column1: # Game profile of Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! (Switch, base game 1.0.0, no update). On Android it plays from a new game to Route 1, catching Pikachu and wild
# Pokémon with buttons, with saves and Continue working (a Galaxy Z Fold 8, see README.md), at 60 fps by default since the frame step stub (30 on the Switch); the Mac runs it at 30
# Game Freak's engine before Sword and Shield's, NVN, SDK 5.4.150, Wwise sound. The provisional profile the survey made (dm/games/profile_guess.py),
# unchanged but for these comments. Shaders: 11,160, from the effect files (.ptcl), main itself, the GFPAK archives and loose BNSH files (see README.md)
# main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB: a 3328 MB heap region
# the NPDM declares 0 MB of system resource: IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, as on Horizon (Big Brain Academy: Brain vs. Brain sets a heap only then)
# used memory for the current rewritten modules, at least the default 64 MB
# 0: the game's own period and the interval 2 it makes from it, 30 fps as on the Switch (the Mac and iOS). With a target the frame step stub (patches.py) makes the game's stored
# frame period the vsyncs the host holds each frame, so game time is real time at 60 and at 30 and the game asks for that interval; Android's default is 60 (android_defaults.txt)
